activity_context.topic_title: Row and Column Operations on Determinants

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating a Determinant After Multiplying a Row by a Number
examples.problem: Suppose $A$ is a $6 \times 6$ matrix and $\det(A) = 32.$ The matrix $B$ is obtained from $A$ by applying the elementary row operation $R_3:= \dfrac{1}{8} R_3$. What is the value of $\det(B)?$
examples.worked_solution:
The row operation applied to $A$ consists of multiplying a row by the number $\dfrac{1}{8}.$

When we do this, the determinant is multiplied by the same number. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =\frac{1}{8}det(A) \\  & =\frac{1}{8}\cdot 32 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Suppose $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix and $det(A)=-15.$ The matrix $B$ is obtained from $A$ by applying the elementary row operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{5}$ (switching the first and the fifth rows). What is the value of $det(B)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since swapping any two rows changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite sign, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =-det(A) \\  & =-(-15) \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$
